Branch cell-1 (worktree scratchpad/wt-c1), tip 5b78d0c, not merged. Not closed: operator verifies.

Known case (cm-27o): `cargo xtask latency --bin <release phonepad from 5b78d0c> calibrate` (an acking viewer, no decoder, through the emulator):
| profile | RTT, jitter, cap, loss | units/s | Mbit/s | send→ack ms p50 / p95 / max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rtt=0 | 0 ms, uncapped | 39.9 | 0.13 | 0 / 1 / 1 |
| rtt=100 | 100 ms, uncapped | 10.7 | 0.11 | 100 / 101 / 101 |
| rtt=200 | 200 ms, uncapped | 8.0 | 0.06 | 200 / 201 / 201 |
| rate=2 | 0 ms, 2 Mbit/s | 8.0 | 1.16 | 244 / 281 / 285 |
PASS added-rtt-100: +100.1 ms (expected 100 ± 15); PASS added-rtt-200: +200.1 ms; PASS stream-cap: 1.161 Mbit/s ≤ 2.1; PASS bulk-cap: 750 KB through the 2 Mbit/s cap measured 2.000 Mbit/s at the receiver (1.9–2.1). Same PASS in two earlier runs (+100.1 / +200.1 each).
Seen red: with the real page as the client the added-RTT clause failed twice (+76.1, then +117.7/+226.4): the page acks at decode and its software decoder adds 5–90 ms that varies with screen content and with RTT. So the known case uses the acking viewer; the page is not a known answer. Clock domain checked: Hyprland's presentation stamp vs CLOCK_MONOTONIC at the Ready event, 335 frames: 31–95 ms, p50 57 ms (positive and bounded, so the clocks match).

Baseline: `cargo xtask latency --bin <release phonepad from 5b78d0c> lan wifi lte bad-lte`. Real page in headless Chromium (412×915 CSS px at 2.625, zoom 2.5, so a 910×1782 view; software decode), uinput mover circling the pointer, 3 s settle + 15 s measured per profile, one instance:
| profile | RTT, jitter, cap, loss | units/s | Mbit/s | drawn/s | stalls > 250 ms (longest gap ms) | capture→send ms p50 / p95 / max | send→ack ms | capture→ack ms | receive→decode ms | decode→draw ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| lan | 0 ms ±0 ms, uncapped, 0% loss | 23.6 | 0.12 | 22.3 | 0 (157) | 90 / 132 / 165 | 8 / 25 / 43 | 103 / 146 / 172 | 10 / 25 / 45 | 0 / 4 / 10 |
| wifi | 10 ms ±0 ms, 50 Mbit/s, 0% loss | 23.3 | 0.11 | 21.8 | 0 (142) | 93 / 137 / 169 | 20 / 47 / 112 | 119 / 169 / 232 | 11 / 29 / 105 | 0 / 4 / 7 |
| lte | 60 ms ±20 ms, 10 Mbit/s, 0% loss | 21.5 | 0.48 | 19.9 | 5 (470) | 93 / 139 / 161 | 72 / 126 / 193 | 169 / 241 / 317 | 10 / 43 / 86 | 0 / 5 / 10 |
| bad-lte | 150 ms ±50 ms, 3 Mbit/s, 1% loss | 5.7 | 1.55 | 4.9 | 25 (877) | 97 / 174 / 198 | 507 / 810 / 1020 | 633 / 895 / 1102 | 29 / 65 / 93 | 0 / 4 / 6 |
An earlier run of the same command, same build, other screen content: lan 54.1 units/s, wifi 52.4, lte 9.9 (28 stalls), bad-lte 7.9 (26 stalls); capture→send p50 27–39 ms. Units/s and capture→send follow what the live screen shows and how busy the render engine is, so compare children against runs taken back to back.

Flagged assumptions (cm-vph): profile delays are RTT, half each way; jitter ±J on RTT = uniform ±J/2 per direction; the cap applies to each direction; loss is per 1448-byte segment per direction, and a lost segment arrives max(200 ms, 2×RTT) later with head-of-line blocking; the emulator queue is 64 segments; test instance on 8771 (the bead says 8766; the operator's safety directive excludes 8765–8767). The "drawn" stall is a gap > 250 ms between drawn reports on the page clock.

Verified by orchestrator 2026-11-10 on merged main d206f09: per-commit gates green (6/6), cargo xtask e2e 24 PASS, cargo xtask latency calibrate: added-rtt-100 +100.0 ms, added-rtt-200 +200.2 ms (expected ±15), stream-cap 0.548 <= 2.1 Mbit/s, bulk-cap 2.000 Mbit/s. Baseline: units/s 22.9 at 0 ms RTT, 9.6 at 100 ms, 8.0 at 200 ms (flow control capped at 4 in flight) — red baseline for .2.
Created issue: Flow control sized to the link (RTT and delivery rate)

Branch cell-2 (worktree scratchpad/wt-c2), tip 6e1f... see git log; not merged, not closed. Commits: 156b887 xtask latency gains viewer / port= / seconds=; ada2a71 xtask views label through projections; 4f36f0c stream: byte window from min RTT and delivery rate (pipe.rs), README, ADR 0004, views regenerated; then a test-only commit pinning the 4 MiB ceiling.

Design: window = max-rate(2 s) x (min-RTT(10 s) + 60 ms), clamped 64 KiB..4 MiB, <= 256 units; a unit into an empty pipe always goes; acks cumulative by id; Unsynced asks for a keyframe only when its pipe is empty (was: on the ack that restored one credit). Flagged assumptions (cm-vph, mine under "accept all"): 60 ms cap, 64 KiB floor, 4 MiB ceiling, 256 units, 10 s / 2 s filter windows, cumulative ack, request on empty pipe. Wire unchanged; timing ledger now 256 entries (was 32).

Known case, calibrate on cell-2: PASS added-rtt +100.3 / +200.3 ms, stream-cap 0.085, bulk-cap 2.000 Mbit/s; units/s 26.3 / 25.8 / 26.0 at 0 / 100 / 200 ms (main baseline 22.9 / 9.6 / 8.0).

A/B, alternating main and cell-2 binaries, port 8781, 15 s per profile, 2 rounds (units/s; longest gap ms; send->ack p95 ms):
acking viewer lte: main 27.7, 23.7 (gaps 458, 480) | cell-2 45.2, 48.1 (gaps 63, 62; p95 80, 80). lan same runs: cell-2 50.3, 48.9.
acking viewer bad-lte: main 7.8, 7.8 (746, 580) | cell-2 47.5, 49.8 (358, 375).
acking viewer bad-lte 60 s: main 7.7, 117 stalls>250, longest 925 | cell-2 50.0, 51 stalls>250, longest 344.
page lte: main 11.9, 10.6 (481, 479) | cell-2 26.7, 50.1 (550, 48; p95 90, 193; receive->decode p95 22, 120).
page bad-lte 60 s: main 7.3, longest 1114 | cell-2 45.5, longest 731 (receive->decode p95 211, max 547 in the 15 s round).
lan: viewer pairs main/cell-2 46.3/50.3, 44.3/48.9, plus 3 lan-only pairs 49.9/48.3, 47.5/58.5, 25.6/26.0; page 43.7/34.1, 49.9/48.9. Pair differences -22% .. +23% on both sides, tracking capture->send in the same rows (e.g. 17 vs 39 ms p50; 115 vs 69 ms p95), so screen-content drift dominates.

Oracle, clause by clause:
- lte >= 55 units/s: UNMET. lte now equals lan (45-50 vs 48-50 in the same runs; main 24-28), but the screen gave <= ~50 units/s in every run, so 55 was not reachable on this content. Needs a run on busier content to decide.
- lte send->ack p95 <= RTT + 60 ms: MET on the acking viewer (80, 80 <= 120); UNMET on the page in round 2 (193), where software receive->decode p95 was 120 ms.
- bad-lte no stall > 500 ms in 60 s: MET on the acking viewer (longest 344); UNMET on the page (731). That the page's 731 is its software decoder is an inference from the viewer run and the page's decode times, not measured directly.
- lan +/-5%: NOT SHOWN as written: pairs scatter -22%..+23% both ways with capture-side drift; no consistent direction (5 of 7 pairs within or above, mean of viewer pairs +5.8%).
Confounds: another agent's phonepad instance (port 8782) ran during the measurement window, sharing the desktop and GPU; content changed between runs.

Mutation: cargo-mutants phonepad-core stream.rs + pipe.rs 63 mutants: 50 caught, 13 unviable, 0 missed (first run missed CEILING 4*1024*1024 -> (4+1024)*1024, test now pins 4_194_304); session.rs+timing.rs 21: 17 caught, 4 unviable (run with --skip owe:: since owe tests fail inside mutants' copied tree, not in the worktree); xtask views/machine/viewer/latency 27: 23 caught, 4 unviable. Planted per rule, all killed: delta while unsynced (3 tests fail), Missed always requests (5), unsynced ack always requests (2), queue cap 0 (2), window pinned to floor (3), min-RTT dropped (2), non-cumulative ack (3), empty pipe refuses (3).
Gates at every commit: fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, test --workspace, xtask check (views-fresh). e2e at tip (binary from 4f36f0c, phonepad code identical to tip): all PASS.
Correction to the comment above: cell-2 tip is 0b68cec (the test-only ceiling commit), on 29520cf; 4 commits: 156b887, ada2a71, 4f36f0c, 0b68cec.

Orchestrator verification 2026-11-10, merged main ac949aa (rebased on the damage-skip change, ADR renumbered 0005): per-commit gates green 4/4, e2e 24 PASS, calibrate: units/s 25.6 / 25.7 / 25.3 at 0 / 100 / 200 ms RTT (was 22.9 / 9.6 / 8.0), added-RTT and cap checks PASS. Left in_progress: the >=55 units/s clause is bounded by screen content (capture rate ~25-50/s on this desktop) and the page clauses by headless Chromium's software decoder; needs an oracle that drives content at >=60 changes/s and a hardware-decoding client (the phone).

Implemented on branch cell-5 (worktree scratchpad/wt-c5), 9 commits 72d9eb6..fca5122, not pushed/merged. Design: each move carries seq s (per connection, from 1); input thread records a phone's last written move inside a seqlock (marks::Marks, generation odd while writing); the sampler keeps a cursorpos reading only if the generation was even and unchanged across copy+query, so a position is credited with exactly the moves written before it (first version without the generation: 4/256 lan messages jumped back, 3 of them by one whole 6 px move double-counted). Pointer message 9 -> 29 bytes: x,y, phone's last applied seq, monitor x,y,w,h. Page (pointer.js, pure, node --test under new page-tests gate): prediction = heard position + uncredited moves, each clamped to the monitor; ring + pan redrawn on the next frame from the last decoded window (pad colour outside it). Oracle: cargo xtask latency touch (CDP Input.dispatchTouchEvent, mover off), tip run seconds=10: handler->redraw p95 lan 0.7 / wifi 0.5 / lte 0.6 / bad-lte 0.5 ms (<=20 PASS); largest backward jump at reconciliation lan 0.0 / wifi 0.0 / lte 0.0 / bad-lte 0.3 px; bad-lte 30 s: p95 0.6 ms, backward max 1.0 px over 676 messages (<=4 PASS). Event-timestamp->redraw p50 ~33 ms on every profile = headless Chromium input pipeline, profile-independent. Known cases: 30 ms busy paint -> redraw FAIL (p95 30.6); page forgetting in-flight moves -> lte jump FAIL (7.8 px). Open for operator: Hyprland libinput adaptive accel also accelerates the phonepad device (2px/16ms x0.9, 10px x1.1, 25px x2.0) so at speed the ring jumps FORWARD at reconciliation (max 45-62 px on bad-lte bursts); making the device flat + retuning page accel is a feel decision, not taken. Optional view margin not built. Feel on cellular: operator. Mutation: cargo-mutants on branch diff 173 mutants, 92 caught/42 missed/39 unviable before follow-up tests; after them touch.rs+cursor.rs 69 caught/12 missed (all CDP/hyprctl I/O shells); JS hand mutants 31/31 killed. ADR 0006.
